Definition: properly, a luminous body or luminary, i.e. (abstractly) light (as an element); figuratively, brightness, i.e. cheerfulness; specifically, a chandelier
BiblicalUsage: The word names a light, a luminous body, and it is the word of the first day's lights. God said let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to divide the day from the night, and to be for signs and for seasons and for days and years, and He made two great lights, the greater to rule the day and the lesser to rule the night. The same word names the oil for the light of the tabernacle, beaten olive oil to cause the lamp to burn always, and the psalm says God made the light and the sun His own.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lights of heaven were made to rule and to mark time, and the lamp of the tabernacle was made to burn always, so God's people never sit in the dark. I hold that the God who set the sun in the sky also keeps a lamp burning before Him, and His light does not go out.
